neutral_facts.value: The accused and the victim lived together for nine years and had two children. The accused had executed an agreement with the victim stating his intention to marry her and had filed an application for marriage registration under the Special Marriage Act. Official documents, including voter lists, showed the victim as the accused's wife. Despite not performing a formal marriage ritual, the accused and the victim cohabited and had a child, leading to the prosecution's claim that the accused had deceived the victim into believing they were married. The accused denied the agreement and claimed the victim was not his wife.

The accused had executed an agreement of marriage and filed an application for registration of their marriage under the Special Marriage Act. In several official documents, she had been shown to be the wife of the accused.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the accused had deceitfully induced the complainant to believe that they were lawfully married, leading to cohabitation and the birth of two children, thereby fulfilling the ingredients of Section 493 of the Indian Penal Code.

quotes.text: There is overwhelming evidence, that the victim and the accused had cohabited for long nine years and during this period, the accused had also executed an agreement of marriage and in addition had filed an application for registration of their marriage under the Special Marriage Act.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the accused did not deceive the complainant into believing they were lawfully married, as there was no formal marriage ceremony or registration, and the complainant was not under the belief of a lawful marriage.

quotes.text: There is no finding by the courts below that by deceit the appellant caused the complainant to believe that she is lawfully married to him.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the principle that a criminal statute must be construed strictly, and all ingredients of the section must be satisfied for an offence to be established.

quotes.text: A criminal statute has to be construed strictly -Unless all its ingredients are satisfied the person cannot be punished, otherwise, there will be violation of Articles 20(1) and 21 of the Constitution of India.
